title: Puebloans - Chaco Regional System
capsule: The Chaco Regional System was the Ancestral Puebloan cultural and economic network centered on Chaco Canyon in the San Juan Basin of present-day New Mexico, functioning as a hub of monumental great-house construction, ritual activity, and long-distance trade from approximately 850 to 1150 CE. Pueblo Bonito, the largest great house, covered nearly two acres and contained over 600 rooms; timber was transported up to 70 miles from distant mountain ranges, and at least 70 outlier communities within a 25,000-square-mile basin were linked by an engineered road network of straight roads up to 30 feet wide. Abandonment of Chaco Canyon began around 1130–1140, driven by a severe 50-year drought, deforestation, and soil degradation; demographic and ceremonial gravity shifted northward to Aztec Ruins and Mesa Verde, with populations eventually coalescing into the historic Pueblo peoples of New Mexico and Arizona.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Chaco Canyon monuments are thoroughly documented archaeologically and Chaco is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; the precise extent of the regional system's political authority versus ritual influence over outlier communities is debated among archaeologists.
